summary: Wasco County, OR: a crow's nest 95 feet up a large tree, dated to 1933; described as abandoned but still there, though a 2013 visitor could not find it.

facts.design: Crow's nest at the 95-foot level of a large tree
facts.status_note: Firelookout.com says abandoned but still there (undated); a July 2013 visitor could not find the crow's nest, and the author says the first person to find the cache did find it

events.note: Firelookout.com says the lookout was established in 1933
Panorama photographs dated November 7, 1933 (Forest Lookouts); the Forest Service survey of lookout panoramas in Oregon and Washington ran from 1933 to 1935
A visit on July 20, 2013 could not find the crow's nest; the post calls the site abandoned

evidence.supports: Crow's nest at the 95-foot level of a large tree
evidence.quote: The lookout consisted of a crow's nest at the 95-foot level of a large tree.

evidence.supports: Managed under the Mt. Hood National Forest
Page title calls the site a tower
Established in 1933; abandoned but still there
evidence.quote: This crows nest tree lookout, established in 1933, is abandoned but still there.

evidence.supports: Forest Service survey of lookouts in Oregon and Washington, 1933 to 1935
evidence.quote: Between 1933 and 1935, the Forest Service in Oregon and Washington undertook an ambitious project to collect high quality panoramic photos from every fire lookout in the region.

evidence.supports: 2013 post describes the site as abandoned
Visit dated July 20, 2013, to look for the remains of the old nest
evidence.quote: to find the remains of the old crow’s nest there

evidence.supports: The author could not find the crow's nest on the July 2013 visit
evidence.quote: Unfortunately I couldn’t find the crow’s nest

evidence.supports: The first person to find the author's cache did find the crow's nest
evidence.quote: The good news is that the first person to find my cache DID find the crow’s nest.

corrections.why: Firelookout.com says the lookout is abandoned but still there (undated); the only later visit we read, in 2013, could not find the nest, so the current state is uncertain

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com says still there, but undated; the 2013 post says abandoned and the nest was not found on that visit, while the author adds that a later finder did locate it. We record standing with a note.
Firelookout.com's page title says tower, but its text and the Forest Lookouts page describe a crow's nest in a tree. The record's platform kind is kept.

notes_for_editor: Duplicate record us-or-bus-point-2 covers the same lookout: different coordinates (45.21087, -121.47275), elevation 1015.9 m, kind tower, status standing, and a Firelookout.com photo. Merge or retire one of the two. Elevation 3,333 ft (1,015.9 m) from Firelookout.com has no facts key here, so it is in this note only. No new photos. Access and visit are left out because no source gives a level. Staffing is left out because no source mentions it. The story describes the historic ladder only in general terms and gives no climbing directions.
